analysis.investment_thesis: Ion Exchange has a decent ROCE (~22%) in a structurally growing water treatment sector, but at an earnings yield of ~5.8% (EBIT INR 297 Cr / EV ~INR 5,106 Cr) it fails the Magic Formula's cheapness test. A massive capex surge (INR 320 Cr in FY25) has cratered FCF to -INR 287 Cr and nearly tripled borrowings — not the time to pay a premium.
key_strengths: Consistent compounding: Revenue CAGR 13.6% and net profit CAGR 32.1% over 9 years — rare operational execution.
Adequate return on capital: ROCE of 22.3% clears my 20% floor, sustained across multiple years.
Secular demand tailwind: Water scarcity and ZLD mandates in Indian industry create durable, government-backed demand.
key_risks: Earnings yield ~5.8% (EBIT/EV) is below my 6% minimum threshold — the stock is not cheap enough for the Magic Formula to reward.
FCF turned sharply negative in FY25 (-INR 287 Cr) as capex tripled to INR 320 Cr; OCF collapsed to INR 32 Cr vs. INR 197 Cr peak.
Borrowings nearly tripled in one year (INR 152 Cr → INR 421 Cr FY24→FY25) — capital intensity rising fast, financing risk elevated.
red_flags: FY25 free cash flow: -INR 287 Cr — the business consumed more cash than it generated in a single year.
CWIP surged from INR 61 Cr to INR 203 Cr — major expansion with uncertain return timeline.
Operating margin of 5.54% is thin and leaves little buffer against project execution risk or input cost inflation.
Promoter holding at only 25.58% — among the lowest I'd want to see; limited skin in the game.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
**Magic Formula verdict: one metric passes, one fails.** EBIT for FY25 is INR 297 Cr on an EV of roughly INR 5,106 Cr (market cap INR 4,932 Cr + net debt INR 174 Cr), giving an earnings yield of ~5.8% — just below my 6% floor. ROCE of 22.3% clears the quality hurdle, and the 9-year net profit CAGR of 32.1% is genuinely impressive. But P/E of 30x and EV/EBITDA of 18.2x reflect a market that already knows this is a good business. The Magic Formula only works when you get quality AND cheapness — here you're paying full price.

**The FY25 capex surge is the central concern.** The company spent INR 320 Cr on capex (vs. INR 120 Cr in FY24), ballooning CWIP to INR 203 Cr. This investment may well generate strong returns — water infrastructure projects in India have long payback periods — but it has temporarily destroyed FCF and required a debt raise that pushed borrowings from INR 152 Cr to INR 421 Cr. Until the new capacity is commissioned and starts generating cash, the stock is in a "show me" phase. I'd watch for OCF recovery and ROIC stability before revisiting.
